reason: Prefetch is a bounded change to the measured K loops, though its benefit is unverified and safe lookahead bounds need proof. Four-tile reuse is the role's distinct reuse hypothesis, but its traversal and pointer remapping raise correctness risk. B-panel packing is also a plausible full-kernel experiment, with added timed packing cost and stride risk. The address-generation and K-schedule proposals depend on confirming a two-K loop body that the supplied baseline does not show; the historical two-step variant also did not promote. Loop-order overlaps the reuse proposal's traversal reversal. The alignment proposal has no supplied misalignment failure, and the transpose paths are high-effort or affect only the non-target fallback. The 64-row panel experiment requires a helper that was not supplied. No proposal has measured evidence of a gain or of exceeding 1800 GFLOP/s.
